headline: US imposes new tariffs on products from Bangladesh and 59 other trade partners over forced labor concerns
summary: The Trump administration has enacted new duties ranging from 10% to 12.5% on goods, effective July 24, citing insufficient measures against forced labor.
details: The Trump administration has imposed new tariffs, ranging from 10% to 12.5%, on products from Bangladesh and 59 other trade partners. This action follows the expiration of a temporary 10% global tariff and is attributed to these countries' alleged failure to take adequate measures against forced labor. The new duties became effective on Friday, July 24.

According to a notice published in the US Federal Register on Thursday, July 23, these new tariffs will apply to 99.4% of goods imported into the United States. However, certain products such as oil-gas, fertilizers, some food items, cars, steel, aluminum, and copper will be exempt from these new duties.

The tariffs have been imposed under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act. This move comes after the US Supreme Court canceled Trump's "reciprocal tariffs" in February, leading the administration to introduce a temporary 10% tariff for 150 days, which has now expired.

US Trade Representative Jamison Greer stated that the United States has strictly prohibited and enforced bans on the import of goods produced with forced labor for nearly a century. He emphasized that it is now time for US trade partners to uphold the same standards.
Under the final decision, a 10% tariff has been imposed on products from 17 countries, including Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, the United Kingdom, Canada, Cambodia, Malaysia, Mexico, and Sri Lanka.

For the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Switzerland, the total tariff rate will be 10% or 12.5%, combining existing duties with the new ones. China and 38 other nations face a 12.5% tariff.

The US administration asserts that the new tariffs are not solely aimed at revenue generation. Instead, their primary objective is to reduce the use of forced labor in global supply chains and ensure fair trade practices worldwide. Countries that have implemented effective anti-labor laws have benefited from comparatively lower tariffs.

Following public hearings, the administration also added certain products to the duty-free list that are not produced in the United States. These include pig iron, specific sugar products, animal and seed-based goods, and particular chemical substances.

headline: Teacher beats 17 students in Naogaon for mocking Argentina football team
summary: The incident occurred at Narchi Government Primary School, leading to protests by parents and locals demanding action against the accused teacher.
details: Teacher Abdus Salam allegedly beat 17 students with an electric wire at Narchi Government Primary School in Naogaon Sadar upazila on Wednesday afternoon. The incident occurred after students reportedly sang a mocking song about the Argentina football team.

The accused, an assistant teacher at the school, entered a fourth-grade classroom where no teacher was present. He became enraged upon hearing the song and proceeded to beat 17 out of 23 students present, including both boys and girls.

The incident sparked outrage among parents and local residents, leading to protests at Narchi intersection near the school on Wednesday night. They demanded a fair investigation and legal action against the teacher.
A fourth-grade student, Shamima Akhter, stated that "Sir Salam supports Argentina. When the team lost, a few of us sang a mocking song in the classroom. Then Sir came and beat us all as he wished."
Local resident Shariful Islam condemned the "unjust torture" of students and called for necessary measures against the teacher to prevent similar incidents in the future.
Teacher Abdus Salam expressed regret and apologized for beating the students, stating he would try to resolve the matter through discussions with parents and school teachers.
Naogaon District Primary Education Officer (Acting) Md. Sanaul Habib stated he was unaware of the incident but would take action according to regulations if a written complaint was filed.
